note: What this file is: how the people test paintings were made (log 34, 16 October 2026, with the user's yes), so they can be matched or made again. Both by Flux 3 edit on fal (blackforestlabs/flux-3/edit-image), 2k, then resized to the plate (1536 x 2730) and lined up with paper-film/tools/align_painting.py against the props' outlines measured by shot_facts.py for the plate's own camera and lens (64.4 degrees). The state picture was made with paper-film/tools/make_state_picture.py. Price on the day: 4.8 US cents a megapixel (twice the plan's figure), about 85 US cents for the two if the pictures sent are charged as well as the one returned (log 32 suggests they are).

paintings.prompt: Repaint image 1 completely as a hand-painted illustration in the exact painting style of image 2: the same visible brush strokes, dark ink outlines, simplified painterly textures on brick, stone, slate and wood, and matte painted finish. Nothing should look like a 3D render or a photograph any more. It is a pit-village street at dusk in 1926. Keep image 1's camera, framing, perspective and every shape, outline, size and position exactly as they are, and keep its pattern of light and dark; change only the brushwork and the colour handling. The people: keep every figure exactly where and as it is, with the same number, size, pose and outline, painted in the same simple way as everything else: dark painted workers in long dark wool work coats and flat caps, in dull browns, greys and near-black, with the same ink outlines. Near the drum there are five men: four seen from behind (one of them bending over the drum to warm his hands, two standing by the lamp post on the right) and one on the left facing us, whose face is lost in deep shadow under the peak of his cap. Far up the street there are six very small dark figures walking away toward the colliery. No faces anywhere: where a face would be there is only dark shadow under the cap, with no eyes, nose, mouth, beard or skin detail; hands are simple dark shapes. Add no people and remove none; add no details to them; they must not look like photographs, statues, shop dummies or toys. Keep: the rusty brazier drum with its open top, dull dark rust-brown, with only a faint orange glow low inside; the red-brick terraces on the left with their chimney stacks; the stone houses, steps and downpipes on the right; every gas lamp with warm amber glass and a small bright mantle inside; the colliery's tall chimney, the two winding wheels and their headgear; the colliery building with its board and its shut iron gates; the flagstone pavement, the kerb, the smooth stone gutter with no steps or ridges, and the sett road. The road, pavement and walls are cool blue-grey dusk, and the brick is weathered and greyed by coal smoke without getting any darker. Warm light stays only where it already is: round the drum, on the nearby pavement, at the lamps and in the few lit windows. Thin parts (the lamp posts and arms, the gate bars, the spokes of the winding wheels, the downpipes) stay thin and exactly in place, or are left out; never thicken them. Where two things meet or nearly meet, keep each edge exactly where it is and never join them: each man and the drum, each man and the next, the men and the lamp post, the far walkers and the colliery gate. Never add: flames, sparks, smoke or steam anywhere (not from the drum, not from any chimney); glows, halos or light rays round any light; puddles, wet shine or reflections; animals or birds; extra props; a moon, stars or bright clouds; new signs or lettering; new or longer shadows.
